question.worked_solution:
To evaluate the given expression, we use PEMDAS.

First, we compute the expression inside the parentheses:

$$
\frac{5}{36}\times 2+(5+1)^{-2}=\frac{5}{36}\times 2+{6}^{-2}
$$

Next, notice that ${6}^{-2}=\frac{1}{{6}^{2}}=\frac{1}{36}.$ So, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{36}\times 2+{6}^{-2} & = \\ \frac{5}{36}\times 2+\frac{1}{36} & = \\ \frac{5}{36}\times \frac{2}{1}+\frac{1}{36} & = \\ \frac{5\times 2}{36\times 1}+\frac{1}{36} & = \\ \frac{10}{36}+\frac{1}{36} & = \\ \frac{10+1}{36} & = \\ \frac{11}{36}\end{aligned}
$$
